topic: Organic Chemistry - Intermolecular Forces and Physical Properties (Vapour Pressure)
question:
Which ONE of the following compounds has the HIGHEST vapour pressure?

A $\text{HCOOH}$
B $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$
C $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$
D $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$
memo:
D $\checkmark\checkmark$

*Rationale: Vapour pressure is inversely related to the strength of intermolecular forces. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (propane) is a non-polar alkane whose molecules are held together only by weak London (dispersion) forces. In contrast, ethanal has stronger dipole-dipole forces, while ethanol and methanoic acid exhibit strong hydrogen bonding. Substances with the weakest intermolecular forces evaporate most readily and therefore have the highest vapour pressure.*

C Ethane and ethanol

memo:

Ethane is saturated; ethanol and ethanoic acid contain oxygen and are therefore not hydrocarbons.*

topic: Chemical Change - Energy and Change (Activation Energy and Heat of Reaction)
question:
Which ONE of the following sets of values for activation energy ($E_a$) and heat of reaction ($\Delta H$) is possible for a reaction?

| | ACTIVATION ENERGY ($E_a$) ($\text{kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$) | HEAT OF REACTION ($\Delta H$) ($\text{kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$) |
|---|---|---|
| A | $100$ | $+100$ |
| B | $50$ | $+100$ |
| C | $50$ | $+50$ |
| D | $100$ | $-50$ |
memo:
D $\checkmark\checkmark$

*Rationale: For an endothermic reaction ($\Delta H > 0$), the activated complex must have higher potential energy than the products, which requires $E_a > \Delta H$. Therefore, options A ($E_a = \Delta H$), B ($E_a < \Delta H$), and C ($E_a = \Delta H$) are physically impossible. For an exothermic reaction ($\Delta H = -50\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$), an activation energy of $100\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$ is completely valid.*

question:
Which ONE of the following changes to the equilibrium conditions will result in an INCREASE in the equilibrium constant, $K_c$?

A Increase in temperature
B Decrease in temperature
C Increase in pressure at constant temperature
D Decrease in pressure at constant temperature
memo:
B $\checkmark\checkmark$

*Rationale: The equilibrium constant $K_c$ is temperature-dependent only; changes in concentration or pressure do not change $K_c$. Because the forward reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H < 0$), decreasing the temperature favours the exothermic (forward) reaction according to Le Chatelier's principle, decreasing the equilibrium concentrations of gaseous reactants and thereby increasing $K_c$.*

A $\text{B}(\text{s})$ is the reducing agent.
B $\text{A}(\text{s})$ is the oxidising agent.

In an electrolytic cell …

A the anode is the positive electrode.
B oxidation takes place at the cathode.
C electrons flow from the cathode to the anode.
D the mass of the anode increases.
memo:

C Platinum
D Vanadium (V) oxide
